description: Rust transactional aggregate fresh query on a local normal Linux node
qualification: Local combined-source node and ephemeral demo trust; one fresh query only
observations: Maintained Rust build captured the source, produced and packaged a real component; explicit Rust transaction demo signing produced the admitted release.
The template generator with the accompanying limit change produced the same captured project files as the tested project.
An authenticated fresh HTTP query returned the empty aggregate and its original view; command count remained zero before and after.
The isolated compiler reported one started and completed job. The node was reaped after clean shutdown and physically retired its state and effect owners.
precedingDiagnostics: An early fixture installed routes after runtime capture and received 403 from a stale selection; installing routes in the metadata session resolved that fixture error.

The one-second original limit expired during cold compilation. At 120 seconds, both 4 MiB and 32 MiB runs returned resource-exhausted; a separate instrumented build identified the canonical input memory reservation as the refusal.
limitations: This is one empty-state Rust query, not a command, intent, conflict, rejection, lost-response, cancellation, or complete language qualification.
The node comes from a verified local combined-source snapshot containing unmerged work; this is not current development, hosted CI, production trust, or an installed distribution.

The component was built with the maintained source recipe before the accompanying template-generator change; a separate byte comparison confirmed that the new generator emits the tested project inputs.
